summary.text: John Elleson is the Republican nominee for Illinois' 9th District and a pastor who also ran for the seat in 2018, losing to Rep. Jan Schakowsky.

He won the March 2026 Republican primary and describes himself as a compassionate conservative; his Ballotpedia survey cites addiction, homelessness, mental health, healthcare and job creation as priorities.

paragraphs.text: Elleson was born in Monmouth, Illinois, and graduated from Christian Life College; BallotReady lists a bachelor's degree in theology from the college in 1985.
He works as a pastor, and BallotReady lists him as pastor of Lakewood Chapel since 1985 and also lists experience as a donut shop owner and baker.
In 2018 he told the Chicago Sun-Times that he pastored a church in Arlington Heights, and his 2018 questionnaire lists a pastoral theology degree from Christian Life College (1985).
His Ballotpedia profile and 2018 survey list no prior elected office, and WTTW's 2026 voter guide lists his occupation as minister and says he has never held a government office.
Elleson was the Republican nominee for the 9th District in 2018 and lost to Jan Schakowsky, 73.5% to 26.5%.
He won the March 17, 2026 Republican primary with 48.9% of the vote, ahead of Paul Friedman (33.6%), Rocio Cleveland and Mark Su.
He describes himself as having decades of service in the community and a proven track record of integrity and results.
